titles: 9 Scam Texts You'll Get This Year (I Wrote Them)

titles: I Ran The "Wrong Number" Scam. Here's Day 1 to Day 40.
The "Wrong Number" Text That Ends With Your Savings
Pig Butchering Explained By An Ex-Scammer (Day By Day)
ep03.desc: "Hi Anna, it's Daniel from the conference." One polite reply to a wrong-number text can turn into the most expensive scam in America. Lenny walks you through it day by day — the photos, the routine, the fake trading profit, the fees — then shows the 5 tells and what to do if someone you love is already in one.

titles: AI Cloned Your Voice. This Is The Call Your Family Gets.
Your Kid Calls Crying. It's Not Your Kid.
How AI Voice Clone Scams Work (And The One Question That Beats Them)
ep04.desc: Your mum gets a call in your voice, crying. You never made it. Lenny shows exactly how the cloned-voice scam works — where the voice comes from, the panic script, the fake officer handoff, the money — plus three more AI tricks (fake boss video calls, deepfake celebrity ads, "AI trading bots") and the family code word that beats them all.
ep04.extra: 📊 Sources: widely reported 2024 Hong Kong deepfake video-call fraud (~US$25M); FTC and FBI guidance on family emergency and impostor scams.

titles: 6 Calls Scammers Make To Your Parents (I Used To Make Them)
"Just Hang Up" Doesn't Work. Here's What Does.
The Phantom Hacker & 5 More Scams Targeting Seniors
ep05.desc: "Just hang up" fails because the scripts are built to stop you hanging up. Lenny, an ex-scammer, plays the 6 calls older people get most — "Grandma, it's me", the government call, the big charge, "you've won", the new friend and the three-person phantom hacker scam — and the 5 things families can set up this weekend that actually work.
ep05.extra: 📊 Sources: FBI IC3 2024 Elder Fraud Report (~$4.9B reported losses by people over 60); FBI warnings on the phantom hacker scam; Social Security Administration scam guidance.

titles: 6 Mind Tricks Scammers Use On Smart People (Ex-Scammer Explains)
You'd Never Fall For A Scam? That's Who I Wanted.

Every scam he ran pushed the same six buttons: the clock, the badge, fear, the favour, everyone else, and the small yes. Learn to see each one, how to switch it off, and a 3-question test that catches almost any scam in five seconds.
